> Written for security, privacy, and IT reviewers evaluating hal for use inside
> an organisation. It states what data leaves the machine, where it goes, what
> hal stores, and how to restrict or disable each of those. Every claim here is
> checkable against the source — see **Verifying these claims** at the end.
>
> Companion documents: `dev/security_model.Rmd` (threat model — what is and
> isn't a security boundary) and `dev/hardening.Rmd` (configuration recipes).

# 1. Summary

hal is an R package that lets a user drive an **already-installed** AI coding
assistant from the R console. It is a client, not a service.

hal itself opens **no remote network connections**. The only socket R opens is
to `127.0.0.1` (the local Positron bridge, vscode backend only). All traffic to
a model provider is made by the vendor's own CLI — GitHub Copilot CLI or
Anthropic Claude Code — running as a local subprocess under the user's own
existing sign-in.

Practically: **if your organisation has already approved GitHub Copilot or
Claude Code for developer use, hal does not introduce a new data-egress
vendor.** It changes which text is sent, not where it goes.

# 2. What hal is not

- Not a model host. It runs no inference and ships no model weights.
- Not a credential store. It holds no provider API key and authenticates to
  nothing. It reads certain credential environment variables locally, but only
  to stop their values being transmitted — see §6.
- Not a telemetry client. It contacts no Anthropic-, GitHub-, or author-operated
  endpoint for analytics, licensing, update checks, or crash reporting.
- Not a security boundary. Its guardrails reduce accidents, not determined
  misuse — see `dev/security_model.Rmd`.

# 3. Data flow by backend

A user selects one backend per session.

| Backend | Transport from R | Who makes the remote call | Destination | Authentication |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vscode` | HTTP to `127.0.0.1:<port>` | Positron / VS Code (`vscode.lm`) | The model behind the user's Positron Copilot sign-in | The user's existing IDE sign-in |
| `copilot` | stdio to a local subprocess | GitHub Copilot CLI | GitHub Copilot API | The user's existing Copilot sign-in |
| `claude` | stdio to a local subprocess | Anthropic Claude Code CLI | Anthropic API | The user's existing Claude subscription sign-in |

In every case hal hands text to a locally-installed vendor tool. It does not
proxy, relay, mirror, or copy that traffic anywhere else.

# 4. What is transmitted

Sent to the selected provider as part of a request:

| Item | When | Default |
|---|---|---|
| The user's prompt | Always | — |
| System prompt (mode-aware, hal-authored) | Always | — |
| Conversation history for the session | Multi-turn (`hal()`) | — |
| A description of R objects in the calling environment — names, classes, dimensions, column names/types | When `use_env = TRUE`, or when auto-detection judges the prompt to reference them | Auto-detect |
| **Results of `eval_r`** — output of R code the model asked to run, which may contain actual data values | When the model calls `eval_r` | Tool enabled |
| **Plot images** (PNG) rendered by `eval_r` | vscode and claude backends | `plot_vision = TRUE` |
| Contents of `hal.md`, if present in the working directory | First turn of a session | Read if present |
| Custom tool results | When the user has registered tools and the model calls them | Opt-in |

The two rows in bold are where **actual data values**, rather than metadata,
can leave the machine. An organisation handling regulated data should treat
`eval_r` as the control point.

# 5. What is never transmitted by hal

- Files not referenced by the prompt or read by a tool the model invoked.
- Environment variables, credential files, SSH keys, or `.Renviron` contents.
- Any identifier of the user, machine, or organisation added by hal.
- Anything at all when no `hal()`, `hal_ask()`, or `hal_do()` call is made.
  Loading the package transmits nothing.

Note the vendor CLI is a separate program with its own behaviour and its own
configuration; this section describes what **hal** sends, not the totality of
what the CLI may send. Review the vendor's documentation for that.

# 6. Credentials

hal stores, reads, and transmits **no** API keys or tokens for any model
provider. Authentication is entirely delegated to the vendor CLI or IDE, which
manages its own credential storage outside hal.

The single secret hal handles is a **local** bearer token for the Positron
bridge (vscode backend). It is generated per bridge launch, read from a
per-user application-data file, sent only to `127.0.0.1`, and is never logged
or printed.

A built-in **credential scanner** inspects outbound prompt text for recognised
secret formats (GitHub PATs, OpenAI/Anthropic keys, AWS keys, Google API keys,
Slack tokens and webhooks, PEM private keys, and generic `key = "value"` pairs).

It additionally reads the values of 21 well-known credential environment
variables — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, and
similar — **for the sole purpose of checking whether those values appear in
text about to be transmitted**. This catches an organisation's real secrets
even when they match no known format. The values are read in-process, compared,
and used only to build the `[REDACTED]` replacement; they are never transmitted,
logged, written to disk, or used to authenticate anything. The watch-list is
`.HAL_SENSITIVE_ENV_VARS` in `R/governance.R`.

> Its default action is `"warn"` — it **notifies but still transmits**. Set
> `credential_action = "block"` (refuse) or `"redact"` (strip) to make it a
> control rather than a notice.

# 7. Local file writes

| Path | Contents | When |
|---|---|---|
| `tempdir()` | IPC request/response JSON, generated MCP server script, tool definitions | While a session with tools is active; removed on `hal_reset()` or session end |
| `hal.md` in the working directory | Project memory, created with a short header the user may edit or delete | Created only in **interactive** sessions, and announced when created |
| Per-user app-data dir | hal-bridge port and token discovery file | Written by the bridge extension, not by hal |

hal writes nothing to system directories, nothing outside these paths, and
nothing at package install or load time.

# 8. Network surface

- **Outbound from R:** `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` only, vscode backend only.
  The host is hardcoded; it is not user- or model-controllable.
- **Inbound:** none. hal opens no listening socket. (The bridge extension, a
  separate component, binds a localhost-only port with token auth.)
- **Subprocesses:** the vendor CLI, plus an R subprocess hosting the MCP tool
  server for the copilot and claude backends.

# 9. Retention and vendor terms

hal retains nothing beyond the local files in §7. Retention, training use, and
regional processing of transmitted text are governed entirely by the agreement
between the organisation (or user) and the model provider — GitHub or
Anthropic. Those terms differ by plan, and enterprise agreements commonly
differ from individual ones.

**hal makes no representation about them.** Consult the provider's current
terms for the specific plan in use.

# 10. Controls available to an administrator

```r
hal_configure(
  permission_policy = "ask",     # confirm before any tool call
  credential_action = "block",   # refuse to transmit detected secrets
  plot_vision       = FALSE,     # never transmit rendered images
  eval_timeout      = 15
)
```

To remove the ability to execute R and transmit data values entirely, restrict
the `eval_r` tool surface via the denylist (`dev/hardening.Rmd` §3). To prevent
all transmission, do not call hal — loading the package is inert.

Backend choice is itself a control: `hal_configure(backend = ...)` pins traffic
to whichever provider the organisation has approved.

# 11. Verifying these claims

A reviewer can confirm the central claims directly, without reading the whole
source. From the package root:

```sh
# Every URL constructed in R. Expect 127.0.0.1 only; the rest are doc links.
grep -rnoE 'https?://[^ "]+' R/

# Every network call site. Expect curl:: in bridge.R and client-vscode.R only.
grep -rn 'curl::' R/

# Credential env-var handling. Expect hits in governance.R ONLY -- that is the
# scanner watch-list described in section 6. Any hit elsewhere would warrant
# scrutiny.
grep -rnE 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|OPENAI_API_KEY|GITHUB_PAT' R/

# Confirm those names are only ever read for comparison, never sent. Expect
# two Sys.getenv() calls inside the scanner -- one to detect, one to redact --
grep -rn 'Sys.getenv' R/governance.R

# Every file-write call site.
grep -rnE 'writeLines|saveRDS|file.create|dir.create' R/
```

The package contains no compiled code, so reviewing the R source is a complete
review of what hal itself can do.
